reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a quasi-periodic oscillation with a robust period of ~183 points (matching the estimated period), manifesting as smooth, asymmetric pulses: each cycle begins with a rapid, near-linear rise (~0.0002–0.0003 per point slope) to a rounded peak (duration ~25–30 points), followed by a slower, concave-down descent (~0.0001–0.0002 per point negative slope) over ~60–70 points to a shallow trough. Peaks consistently reach 2.9–4.0 robust-standardized units; troughs hover near −0.5 to −1.0, rarely dipping below −1.1. Baseline level drifts mildly across windows (median shifts from −0.29 to +0.16), but local morphology remains stable—peak width, ascent/descent asymmetry, and curvature (~0.013–0.014) are highly conserved. Noise is low: roughness stays ~0.030–0.032, indicating minimal high-frequency jitter. Amplitude at the 90th percentile ranges 3.8–4.5, reflecting slight scaling variation but no abrupt outliers. All candidates show clean, non-truncated cycles at boundaries, confirming full-cycle inclusion. The consensus normal is defined by this repeating pulse shape—not absolute y-level—so queries should be aligned by phase and cycle count before comparison.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 1 or 2 for query windows of ~3 cycles (most representative morphology); use reference 0 for single-cycle alignment or when query shows only one pulse; use reference 3 when query spans ≥4 cycles to assess long-term stability. Always match by cycle count first, then align on peak timing—not absolute x-index. If a query shows steeper ascent, sharper peaks, or truncated troughs, it deviates from consensus regardless of baseline level.
